papers.title: An explicit upper bound on the number of subgroups of a finite group
papers.read_scope: Sections 2–4; all arithmetic statements and final bound
papers.assessment: Theorem 1.1 bounds subgroup counts by 7.3722*r^(log_2(r)/4+1.5315). The per-prime arithmetic uses S(p,a); the explicit remaining exponent and constants prevent identifying this theorem with the source arithmetic inequality.

papers.title: On the maximum number of subgroups of a finite group
papers.read_scope: Sections 2, 4; proofs in Sections 7.2–7.4; remaining statements scanned
papers.assessment: Theorem 1.1 is the sharp subgroup bound c(2)*r^(log_2(r)/4). Arithmetic reductions in Lemmas 4.1–4.3 concern a different function involving S(p,a), c(p) and normalizer factors; their reductions assume p_1=2, a_1>=2, ell>=3. No exact full source implication was identified.

papers.authors: Lorenzo Guerra, Fabio Mastrogiacomo and Pablo Spiga
papers.title: Counting subgroups of a finite group containing a prescribed subgroup
papers.read_scope: Section 3 arithmetic observations and final assembly; theorem statements
papers.assessment: Theorem 1.1 bounds intervals by 7.3722*[R:T]^(log_2([R:T])/4+1.8919). Lemmas 3.3–3.4 and Proposition 3.5 reuse per-prime S(p,c) estimates. No exact source inequality or its exception set was located.

papers.title: Sharp bounds for intervals in finite subgroup lattices
papers.read_scope: Theorems 1.1/1.3, Corollary 1.2 and weighted packing consequences Sections 2–4
papers.assessment: The sharp interval bound uses a least prime divisor, weighted generating-tuple packing and a discrete Gaussian sum. It does not state the source prime-power product inequality or the exceptions 36,72,900; no full source implication was identified.
